### The ranges' sources

- **Heat the mixture can release at its lambda**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), §4.9.4 and fig. 4-23 (combustion efficiency): at phi 1.1 the oxygen limits the release; the CO and H2 in the products carry 7 to 12 % of the fuel's heat (eq. 4.69's chemistry, worked in causes.md)
- **Released into the gas**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), fig. 4-23 with §11's unburned HC (2 to 3 % at full load)
- **Walls, in the cylinder, all**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), §12.1 and table 12.1: 17 to 26 % to the coolant at full power, less the exhaust port's 3 to 5 % and friction's share
- **Gross indicated work**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), §5.7 fig. 5-9 and §15 (the real engine is some 0.8 of the fuel-air cycle: 0.42 to 0.45 at r 10 to 11, phi 1.1); fig. 15-? measured full-load indicated efficiencies
- **Pumping**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), §13.4: 0.1 to 0.6 bar at wide-open throttle
- **Friction (gross - pumping - brake)**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), §13.6 (Chen and Flynn)
- **Brake**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), table 12.1: 25 to 28 % at maximum power; to 31 at peak torque
- **Exhaust, sensible enthalpy above the inlet's**: Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals (1988), table 12.1: 34 to 45 % at maximum power
- **First law's residual (released - walls - work - net enthalpy - dU)**: the probe's own check
